1 · The data

A complete monthly panel over four kinds of water

Every sampling point has exactly one row per month. Eighteen water-quality inputs are grouped into field measurements (Temp, pH, Turbidity, EC, DO, SS), lab measurements (Br, BOD, COD, NH3-N, TOC, SUVA, Aromaticity, Mol. weight) and LC-OCD carbon fractions (Biopolymer, Humic substances, Building blocks, LMW neutrals). The outputs are trihalomethane and haloacetic-acid formation potentials in mg/L.

2 · Key EDA findings

Organic carbon quantity, season and place

  • Both targets are log-normal (medians 0.08 mg/L, range 0.007–0.55) and correlate with each other at Spearman 0.67. All modelling is on log10.
  • Humic substances and TOC are the strongest predictors: Spearman 0.66–0.78 with the targets. Bromide is weak on its own (≈0.2) and adds little once TOC is known.
  • Site and month each explain more variance than any single predictor: site η² up to 0.59 for HAAFP, date η² up to 0.47 for THMFP on river rows. A random train/test split would leak both.
  • River water carries about twice the formation potential of reservoirs and treated water. Along the main stem, values rise downstream and peak around the Goryeong reach in summer.
  • Treatment removes roughly half at coagulation/settling, ozonation slightly raises it, and GAC or F/A brings finished water to 0.03–0.05 mg/L.
  • Summer 2018 is anomalous: main-stem monthly medians reached 0.32 mg/L against ≤0.21 in every other month, and one tributary event (Hoecheon, Aug 2018) holds record values for several variables.
  • Data-quality handling: 29 Korean non-detect strings set to NaN with flags, 4 zero placeholders in the UV/size trio removed, blank site codes for two treatment trains recovered from names.
3 · Modelling

Three feature tiers, four ways of holding data out

Features were added in nested tiers so the value of each kind of information could be measured. Every model was tuned by a nested random search whose inner folds share the outer scheme's grouping, so held-out months and sites never leak into tuning. Ridge, HistGradientBoosting and XGBoost were compared against median, site-median and persistence baselines.

4 · Best models

One recommendation per target

Selection rule fixed before the experiments: the highest mean R² over the month and site schemes. Both winners are ridge regressions on network-aware features; the round-0 XGBoost models are kept in models/ for the chemistry-only case.

Ridge regression (median impute → scale → RidgeCV) on feature set t3_basin · saved as models/THMFP_t3_basin_ridge.joblib

Core-10 chemistry (log-scaled), site group, treatment stage, main-stem position, month, fold-fit site encoding, last month's THMFP / TOC / HS at the site, upstream and downstream same-month values, and the leave-one-out same-month mean of the other river sites and of the site's own group.

Up from 0.53 / 0.70 / −0.17 (round-0 XGBoost). The basin mean carries the shared monthly signal, which is what let a linear model overtake the trees and extrapolate into the summer-2018 anomaly.

Ridge regression (median impute → scale → RidgeCV) on feature set t4_all · saved as models/HAAFP_t4_all_ridge.joblib

Everything in the THMFP set plus LC-OCD fractions as ratios to TOC, Temp × log TOC, the sparse extras (COD, SS, DO, BOD, NH3-N, SUVA, Aromaticity, Mol. weight, NaN-flagged) and last month's THMFP.

Up from 0.61 / 0.68 / 0.52. Humic substances remain the top chemistry driver; the downstream and upstream same-month HAAFP values rank alongside it. For a brand-new site with no network context the chemistry-only XGBoost (site R² 0.72) is still the safer pick.

5 · Caveats

What to keep in mind

  • One seasonal cycle. Sixteen months is a single year plus four; the forward test is one anomalous summer. Expect degradation in unusual years and retrain as months arrive.
  • Network features need the network. Basin, group, downstream and plant-raw features assume the other sites were sampled the same month. Without them, fall back to the chemistry-only models.
  • Units are assumed (mg/L for the targets, µg/L C for LC-OCD fractions, µS/cm for EC); the workbook does not state them. Detection limits for the 29 non-detects are also unknown.
  • One model-side change slipped into round 1: ridge gained a missing-value indicator, which raised its own baseline. Feature gains are measured against the re-run baseline, so they are like-for-like.
  • Not yet tried: ridge–XGBoost blending, a joint two-target model, prediction intervals, robust losses.
Reproduce: uv sync → uv run python -m src.train --all → uv run python -m src.train --ablation → uv run python -m src.interpret. Notebooks notebooks/eda.ipynb and notebooks/modeling.ipynb render every figure. Repository: github.com/thanhtrunghuynh93/Korean_river.
